paras: The killing of George Wallace was the shooting of a young man by a squad of Arkansas state militia near Mound City, across the river from Memphis, on a Saturday in January 1869. Wallace fled on meeting the squad while carrying provisions to his mother and was pursued and killed instantly. The Memphis Appeal reported it as a murder by "Clayton's bandits" and reprinted the item in August 1888 as part of a record of "Despotic Republican Rule" in Arkansas.

In January 1869 the Appeal ran a series of dated items on the militia of Governor Powell Clayton, which it described as plundering along the river and torturing and shooting prisoners at Marion. Wallace, who lived near Mound City and was the sole support of his mother, had fled to Memphis when the militia first came to Marion and stayed there several days.

Hearing on a Friday that his mother was in need, Wallace crossed over to bring her provisions. According to the Appeal, on his way to the house he met a squad of militia and, "fearing harm," turned and ran. The squad pursued him, fired, and killed him instantly; the paper gave no number for the squad, no names of the shooters, and no reason on their part for firing. The account does not state Wallace's race.
No report of an inquest, arrest, or other official response to the killing appears in the coverage.

The only known account is a short paragraph headed "January 25" under the line "MORE KILLING," which called the death a "murder" and the shooters "Clayton's bandits." It survives in the coverage through the Appeal's own republication on August 28, 1888, which presented its 1869 items as "additional proofs" of "the desperate lengths to which Gov. Powell Clayton went." The 1888 headlines spoke of "Red-Handed Militia Over-Awing and Oppressing the People" and set the reprint alongside presidential campaign news on the same page. No other paper's report of the killing, and no account from the militia, was found.

reader.title: Killing of George Wallace (1869)
bases: A squad of state militia under Gov. Clayton pursued and shot an unarmed man who fled from them, with no crowd reported (A3); the Appeal itself called the militia 'bandits' and a 'mob called militia' (A2, A3).
The only account is one 1869 Memphis Appeal paragraph, known through the Appeal's own 1888 reprint (A2, A3); no second report was found.

accounts.label: Memphis Appeal (1869, reprinted 1888)
accounts.gist: Wallace, fearing harm, fled on meeting a squad of militia while carrying provisions home, and the squad pursued, fired on and killed him instantly.

framing.detail: The 1869 entry called the killing 'murder' under the head 'MORE KILLING' and the militia 'Clayton's bandits'; the 1888 reprint framed the column as proof of 'Despotic Republican Rule' and 'Red-Handed Militia' during the presidential campaign season.

info: A Saturday in January 1869, reported in an Appeal entry dated January 25, 1869; the 1888 reprint gives the original year only in its introduction
